title: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Study Guide
description: CompTIA Network+ (N10-009, launched 20 June 2024) is the vendor-neutral networking certification. It is up to 90 questions in 90 minutes, mixing multiple choice, drag-and-drop and performance-based questions, with 720 on a 100–900 scale to pass. It covers networking concepts, implementation, operations, security and troubleshooting — addressing, routing and switching basics, wireless, cloud connectivity, and the systematic troubleshooting method the exam keeps returning to.
audience: Help desk and support technicians moving toward infrastructure work, career changers who want networking fundamentals that are not tied to one manufacturer, and anyone whose employer or contract asks for a vendor-neutral credential. CompTIA suggests around nine to twelve months of networking experience; in practice plenty of people pass it as a second certification after A+, with lab time standing in for the job.
why_get_it: Network+ is the most recognized vendor-neutral networking certification available. Unlike CCNA, which is Cisco-specific, Network+ knowledge applies across vendors—Cisco, Juniper, HP, Palo Alto, and cloud networking alike. It covers a broad foundation: network topologies, TCP/IP, routing and switching concepts, wireless, security, and troubleshooting methodology. For IT support professionals, it demonstrates competence beyond basic helpdesk skills. For career changers, it provides structured knowledge that accelerates understanding of any IT environment. It is also a natural prerequisite for CompTIA Security+ and other security certifications, as many of the concepts tested in security exams assume solid networking knowledge.
when_to_get_it: Network+ is worth taking when you want the vocabulary and the troubleshooting discipline before specialising, or when a job posting names it. It sits naturally between A+ and Security+, and it is the cheaper, broader option. The honest comparison is with CCNA: Network+ is easier and applies anywhere, while CCNA goes considerably deeper and appears in far more networking job postings — if networking is the destination rather than a stepping stone, many people skip straight to CCNA. N10-009 is expected to retire around 2027.
salary_note: Network+ holders in junior network technician and IT support roles typically earn $55K–$70K. With experience and additional certs (CCNA, Security+), salaries commonly reach $75K–$95K. The cert is frequently a stepping stone rather than a destination—the salary jump comes when it is paired with experience or higher certs.
exam_format: Multiple choice, drag-and-drop, and performance-based questions. Maximum 90 questions.
exam_questions: Up to 90 questions (CompTIA does not publish exact count)
recertification_note: Network+ is valid for 3 years. Renew by earning 30 CEUs through CompTIA's Continuing Education program, or by passing a higher-level CompTIA exam before expiration.

items: OSI and TCP/IP models in depth
IP addressing and subnetting (IPv4 and IPv6)
Common ports and protocols (DNS, DHCP, HTTP/S, FTP, SSH)
Routing concepts and protocols (static routes, RIP, OSPF concepts)
WAN technologies and connectivity (MPLS, fiber, broadband)
Network hardware: routers, switches, firewalls, access points
Virtual networking and cloud network concepts
Change management and configuration management basics
Backup, recovery, and high availability concepts
Network access control and port security
Network diagnostic tools (ping, traceroute, nslookup, netstat)

study_steps.title: Review the official exam objectives
study_steps.description: Download the N10-009 exam objectives from CompTIA's website. The current version was updated to reflect modern networking realities including cloud and automation concepts. Map your existing knowledge against the objectives to identify where you need the most work.

study_steps.title: Study networking fundamentals first
study_steps.description: If IP addressing and the OSI model are not already solid, start there. Subnetting in particular needs to be reliable under exam pressure. Use free subnet calculators to check your work, but learn to do it manually—the exam includes questions where understanding the process matters.

study_steps.title: Work through a full course
study_steps.description: Professor Messer's free Network+ course covers every objective and is the go-to resource for most candidates. Jason Dion's Udemy course is a strong paid alternative with scenario practice and performance-based question prep. Complete your chosen course before taking practice exams.

study_steps.title: Build hands-on skills with a home lab or simulator
study_steps.description: Network+ includes performance-based questions that require practical knowledge. Cisco Packet Tracer (free) or GNS3 let you practice configuring switches, setting up VLANs, and tracing connectivity issues. Even 30 minutes of hands-on time per study session significantly improves retention.

study_steps.title: Take full-length practice exams
study_steps.description: Jason Dion's and Total Seminars' Udemy practice tests are widely regarded as the most accurate available. Take your first practice exam after completing your course, identify weak domains, review those topics, then take additional exams until you are scoring 80%+ consistently.

study_steps.title: Schedule and sit the exam
study_steps.description: Book through Pearson VUE. Performance-based questions appear first—budget extra time for them and do not get stuck. If a PBQ is unclear, flag it and return after completing the multiple choice section. The exam is 90 minutes; time management matters.

free_resources.name: Professor Messer – N10-009 Network+ Course (Free)
free_resources.note: The most widely used free Network+ resource. Clear, objective-aligned, and updated for N10-009. A reliable study backbone for most candidates.

free_resources.name: CompTIA Network+ Exam Objectives (N10-009)
free_resources.note: Download the official objectives PDF. This is the authoritative guide to what is and is not on the exam.

free_resources.name: Cisco Packet Tracer
free_resources.note: Free network simulation tool from Cisco. Requires a free Networking Academy account. Excellent for practicing subnetting, VLANs, and routing concepts.

free_resources.name: r/CompTIA on Reddit
free_resources.note: Read recent exam pass posts for insight into what current candidates faced on test day.

paid_resources.provider: Udemy – Jason Dion Network+ (N10-009) Full Course
paid_resources.best_for: Most candidates – full N10-009 video coverage with scenario practice and PBQ prep
paid_resources.note: Jason Dion's N10-009 course is one of the most enrolled Network+ courses on Udemy, with a downloadable study guide and practice exam included. Frequently on sale.

paid_resources.provider: Total Seminars – CompTIA Network+ (N10-009) Practice Exams
paid_resources.best_for: Final exam preparation with full-length N10-009 practice tests from a different question bank than your course
paid_resources.note: The TOTAL: CompTIA Network+ practice exams (Mike Meyers' Total Seminars team). A second question bank to confirm readiness before booking.

paid_resources.provider: Mike Meyers – CompTIA Network+ All-in-One Exam Guide (McGraw-Hill)
paid_resources.best_for: Candidates who prefer reading, or want a comprehensive written reference alongside video content
paid_resources.note: The All-in-One series is the most complete single-volume Network+ reference available. Detailed without being inaccessible.

paid_resources.best_for: Hands-on practice terminating, crimping, and testing real Ethernet cable — the physical-layer skills Network+ actually tests
paid_resources.note: Optional but valuable. Network+ covers cabling standards and termination; practicing on real RJ45 connectors makes those topics stick.

voucher_links.label: Buy Network+ Exam Voucher – CompTIA Store
voucher_links.note: Verify current pricing on CompTIA's official store. Bundle options with retake insurance are worth considering for first-time test-takers.

faq.question: Is Network+ harder than A+?
faq.answer: Yes, generally. Network+ goes deeper into networking concepts, requires more subnetting knowledge, and includes performance-based questions that require practical skill. A+ is broader across IT support topics but less depth per topic. Most candidates find Network+ the step up in rigor.

faq.question: Should I get Network+ or CCNA?
faq.answer: Depends on your goal. If you want to work specifically in enterprise networking with Cisco equipment, CCNA is the stronger credential and goes deeper. If you want vendor-neutral knowledge or a stepping stone to security certifications, Network+ is the right choice. Many professionals hold both.

faq.question: How long does it take to study for Network+?
faq.answer: Most candidates spend 6 to 10 weeks studying part-time. Candidates with existing networking or IT experience may be ready in 4 to 6 weeks. Those new to IT should plan for 8 to 12 weeks and invest time in hands-on practice, not just video watching.

faq.question: What jobs does Network+ qualify me for?
faq.answer: Network Technician, IT Support Specialist, Help Desk Analyst (with networking focus), Junior Network Administrator, and NOC Technician roles frequently list Network+ as a requirement or strong preference. It also satisfies a baseline for many government IT roles.

faq.question: Is Network+ enough to get a job in networking?
faq.answer: It helps significantly, but pairing it with hands-on experience—even a home lab—improves your odds considerably. The cert gets you through resume filters; the interview requires demonstrated competence. Network+ plus Cisco Packet Tracer lab work is a strong entry-level combination.

faq.question: What is the passing score for Network+?
faq.answer: The passing score for N10-009 is 720 on a scale of 100 to 900. CompTIA uses scaled scoring.
